item.title: Cyclone Arnab: Andhra, Odisha prepare to evacuate people ahead of landfall
item.description: Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal before intensifying into a cyclonic storm, is expected to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh state by Wednesday morning ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two states along India's eastern coast were preparing to evacuate thousands of people ahead of Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall on Wednesday, as one of them said it would close schools in some districts for two days. Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal before intensifying into a cyclonic storm, is expected to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh state by Wednesday morning, with gusts of as much as 140 kph (87 mph), India's weather office said. The cyclone will probably intensify further, it added. The weather system is expected to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to Andhra Pradesh's northern and central coastal districts, and southern regions of neighbouring Odisha. Andhra Pradesh has called for boats at sea to return ashore and ordered speedy restoration of power in case of disruptions. A senior Andhra Pradesh disaster management official told Reuters on Monday the state government had identified 570,000 people as vulnerable and evacuations would start on Monday evening. Odisha's government announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday, and said it was preparing to move residents of low-lying areas to cyclone shelters. The Bay of Bengal is one of the world's major regions for tropical cyclones.

item.title: Apple 'Pro and tell' event this week: OLED MacBook Pro, iPad mini expected
item.description: Apple's 'Pro and tell' event this week is expected to feature a MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen and an iPad mini with an OLED display, alongside other product updates ...
item.dc:creator: Harsh Shivam
item.content:encoded: Apple is set to announce new products this week, with a redesigned MacBook Pro featuring an OLED touchscreen expected to be the main highlight of its upcoming “Pro and tell” event. The company could also unveil an updated entry-level MacBook Pro, a refreshed iMac and a new iPad mini. According to a report by 9to5Mac, Apple’s “Pro and tell” event will take place in Los Angeles on October 28 at 10 am Pacific Time (10:30 pm IST). The company announced the event last week, with its Senior Vice President of Marketing, Greg Joswiak, teasing the launch in a post on X on October 19, writing, “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week”.ALSO READ: Apple's iPhone Duo hits stores in face of short supply, high demandThis will be Apple's second product launch this month, following its October 13 “Welcome home” event, where it unveiled the HomeView smart display, HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K.Apple ‘Pro and tell’ event: What to expectMacBook Pro with OLED touchscreenThe main announcement is expected to be a redesigned MacBook Pro with an OLED display and touch support. Apple is reportedly preparing 14-inch and 16-inch models powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which were introduced earlier this year. According to MacRumors, citing Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the new laptops will be lighter than the current models and replace the display notch with a Dynamic Island interface, similar to the feature available on Apple's iPhones. The change would bring a new display design to the MacBook Pro range alongside the shift to OLED technology. The touchscreen is expected to work alongside the existing keyboard and trackpad, rather than replace them. Apple is also reportedly developing changes to macOS to accommodate touch input, including controls that adapt to how a user interacts with the display.ALSO READ: Apple AirPods 5 review: Great call quality and ANC, but not for everyoneThe OLED MacBook Pro models could cost more than the current versions, with the more expensive display technology and touchscreen adding to production costs. According to MacRumors, the starting prices in the US could be up to $500 higher than those of the existing models. Apple is expected to position these laptops above its current MacBook Pro models, which could remain on sale for some time.14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chipApple could also introduce an updated entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by its next-generation M6 chip. Unlike the OLED models, this version is not expected to receive a major design change. The current entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro uses Apple's M5 chip. An upgrade to the M6 could bring improvements in processing performance and power efficiency, while retaining the existing display technology and overall design.iMac with M6 chipAn updated iMac is also expected at the event. The current 24-inch iMac uses Apple's M4 chip, and the next version is expected to move to the M6 processor. The new model is not expected to receive a major design overhaul. Apple could focus on the processor upgrade and introduce new colour options.iPad mini with OLED displayApple could also refresh the iPad mini with an OLED display and a new processor. The current iPad mini uses an LCD panel, so the reported switch to OLED would bring the smaller tablet closer to the display technology used in the iPad Pro range. The updated iPad mini could use Apple's A20 Pro chip and feature a front-facing camera repositioned for landscape use. Other expected changes include a redesigned speaker system and improved water resistance.

L&T Technology Services, Nokia sign deal to support engineering in India The contract brings together LTTS' engineering capabilities with Nokia's telecommunications technology work

LTTS will establish a dedicated Offshore Development Center (ODC) in India to support Nokia's engineering and R&D initiatives | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 12:41 PM IST

Listen to This Article

L&T Technology Services on Monday announced a five-year contract with Nokia to support engineering and research and development activities in India. The contract brings together LTTS' engineering capabilities with Nokia's telecommunications technology work, according to a release. The release did not divulge the size or financial details of the contract. Under the agreement, LTTS will support Nokia R&D programs across areas, including product engineering, software development, system integration, and product support. LTTS will establish a dedicated Offshore Development Center (ODC) in India to support Nokia's engineering and R&D initiatives. Also Read

The ODC brings data-center-grade compute and AI-infrastructure engineering to next-generation telecom solutions. LTTS will also create a dedicated engineering team in India to support Nokia's technology center globally, with work spanning areas such as 5G networks, intelligent automation, AI-driven operations and AI infrastructure.

LTTS will work with Nokia's global R&D teams through an integrated operating model. The engagement will cover research and development, product engineering, new product development, embedded systems, software development, system integration, and ongoing support. Vivek Jaiswal, Senior Vice President of Engineering at Nokia, said, "India is an important innovation hub for Nokia, and LTTS is a critical partner that will bring engineering expertise and mechanisms that will help us expand our R&D footprint and accelerate innovation in this strategically important geography."   Alind Saxena, Executive Director and President, Strategic Initiatives & Growth Markets at L&T Technology Services noted this strategic engagement represents a significant milestone for LTTS and the technology segment.

"It reflects the trust that leading technology innovators place in our engineering intelligence approach and deep-tech engineering expertise. This collaboration also aligns strongly with LTTS' Lakshya 31 Big Bet around next gen compute and AI infrastructure, an area that will be fundamental to the evolution of future communication networks and intelligent datacenters," Saxena said.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout

Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 8:42 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity.   Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses.   It was not immediately clear from Musk's post what he meant by the deal being "closed" or whether investors had agreed to pricing for the debt.   "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter," Musk said in the post.

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen. Also Read

Musk says he was behind Starlink speed curbs after Ukraine service restored

Ukraine says Starlink speed limits lifted after disruptions to military ops

Musk's donations top $445 million in push for Republicans in US midterms

Trump says Musk restored Ukraine's Starlink access, dodges call question

Trump admin offers mixed messages on limits to Ukraine's Starshield access

Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of Nvidia artificial intelligence chips.   The funding highlights the enormous capital requirement of the AI boom, as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out the computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.   Musk said debt markets "have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers."

As a result, he predicted neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, and later said SpaceX won't buy any neoclouds, calling it "pointless."   Unlike larger cloud firms that serve a broad range of industries, neoclouds such as Nebius and CoreWeave mostly focus on tech customers and offer capacity tailored for AI technology.   Investors have started betting against US neocloud and data center companies, after fears that their debt-fueled AI buildout was becoming unsustainable sparked a selloff.  AI investment, chip manufacturing   SpaceX's revenue climbed 161% from a year ago to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX's heavy investment in AI was paying off.

The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink satellite internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service.   Terafab, the chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla in Austin, should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year as it aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028.   Musk told investors in a conference call last week that a merger of his two companies would be "a good idea," citing growing overlap between them.   Prior to its blockbuster IPO, SpaceX listed "manufacturing our own GPUs" among the substantial capital expenditures it is undertaking in its S-1 statement, warning prospective investors of its big spending plans to develop AI and other technologies.
